Title: Template helper isolation and pack immutability decision
Purpose: Finish isolating duplicated template-to-editor mapping rules and make the pack-caching/immutability tradeoff explicit and safe.
Deliverables: One shared owner for role-draft and artifact-expectation mapping rules instead of repeating that logic across catalog, library, and projection services.
A short design note that explicitly chooses one of two safe directions: keep the pack scoped because the graph is mutable, or make the pack truly immutable and safe for broader caching.
No introduction of a shared mutable singleton pack graph without immutability or defensive cloning.
Regression proof that catalog/library/projection behavior still agrees after helper extraction.
ReviewQuestions: Do role/artifact mapping rules now have one clear owner?
Is the pack caching/immutability decision now explicit, justified, and thread-safe?
Did helper isolation reduce duplication without widening into unrelated template rewrites?
CorrectiveOnFailure: If the change introduces shared mutable cross-scope state or still leaves the same mapping rules duplicated in multiple services, stop and open the template-isolation corrective playbook.
